title: Mutual effects of accelerated carbonation and GGBFS stabilization on the mechanical performance and heavy‐metal immobilization of iron ore tailings
content:
Abstract

Pressurized CO2 carbonation combined with ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS) was evaluated as a low-carbon strategy for valorizing iron ore tailings. Compacted tailings containing 0–9 wt % GGBFS were carbonated at 0.5–1.5 bar for 2–8 h and examined by UU triaxial testing, SEM–EDS, TGA, TCLP, and LCA. At 200 kPa confinement, untreated tailings reached 503 kPa peak deviator stress, compared with 780 kPa after carbonation alone at 1.5 bar and 1058 kPa with 9 wt % GGBFS, corresponding to increases of 55% and 110%, respectively. Surface porosity decreased from 43.3% to 28.5%, Ca content increased from 9.38 to 20.82 wt %, and TGA supported carbonate-bearing product formation and matrix densification. The combined treatment reduced leaching of all investigated metals by 70.0–90.5% relative to untreated tailings. Under the adopted system boundary and assumptions, LCA indicated up to 75% reductions in global warming potential and energy demand relative to cement-based stabilization.
